question.prompt:
The sum

\[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^3 + 6k^2 + 8k}\]

can be expressed as \(\dfrac{a}{b},\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(a + b?\)

solutions.title: Cancel fractions two places apart
solutions.explanation:
The denominator factors into three factors spaced two apart, suggesting a difference whose shifted terms will cancel:
\[
k^3+6k^2+8k=k(k+2)(k+4).
\]
Indeed, subtracting two fractions gives
\[
\frac{1}{k(k+2)}-\frac{1}{(k+2)(k+4)}
=\frac{(k+4)-k}{k(k+2)(k+4)}
=\frac{4}{k(k+2)(k+4)}.
\]

Define \(u_k=1/[k(k+2)]\). Each summand in the question is therefore \(\tfrac14(u_k-u_{k+2})\). If \(S_N\) denotes the sum of the first \(N\) summands, then for \(N\ge2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_N
&=\frac14\bigl[(u_1+\cdots+u_N)-(u_3+\cdots+u_{N+2})\bigr]\\
&=\frac14(u_1+u_2-u_{N+1}-u_{N+2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every term appearing in both lists cancels, leaving only these endpoints.

As \(N\) grows, \(u_{N+1}\) and \(u_{N+2}\) become arbitrarily small because their denominators grow without bound. Hence the infinite sum equals
\[
\frac14\left(\frac{1}{1\cdot3}+\frac{1}{2\cdot4}\right)
=\frac14\left(\frac13+\frac18\right)
=\frac{11}{96}.
\]
Since \(11\) and \(96\) are relatively prime, the requested value is
\[
a+b=11+96=\boxed{107},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
